SOFTWARE ENGINEER I
About the Firm
Firm Mission
“Achieving Client Success through Research and Technology”
Los Angeles Capital, the “Firm”, is a global equity manager of assets for leading institutions around the world. The Firm is recognized as a pioneer in dynamic equity management, utilizing proprietary technology to engineer equity portfolios that adapt to today’s equity market. The Firm’s senior investment professionals have worked together for three decades developing models for measuring and forecasting return and risk of global equity securities. The Firm manages approximately $40.1 billion as of December 31, 2025, across a wide variety of public equity strategies designed to meet institutional client return and risk objectives. The Firm has been ranked for seven years in a row by Pensions and Investments as one of the “Best Places to Work in Money Management.” The Firm’s working environment places a strong focus on teamwork and values work-life balance. The Firm offers a competitive compensation package that includes health care plans, 401(k), and top-tier benefits. The Firm is 100% employee-owned through a holding company structure and seeks to retain and motivate employees’ long term. Los Angeles Capital firmly believes the quality and commitment of the individuals are vital to the success of the Firm, ensuring that client expectations are exceeded.
Position Overview
Reporting to the Associate Director in the Quantitative Investment Platform (QIP) team within Research, the Software Engineer will help design, build, and maintain the Python applications, services, and tooling that power the Firm’s investment platform. Working alongside more senior engineers, this person will write production code — APIs, domain logic, automation, and supporting libraries — with a strong emphasis on clean, well-tested, maintainable software. This is a strong fit for someone early in their career who wants to develop real depth in software engineering inside a quantitative investment firm.
Key Job Responsibilities
Design, build, and maintain Python applications and services that support the firm’s research and investment process, with guidance from senior engineers
Write clean, well-tested, maintainable code following team standards: type hints throughout, small focused functions, and clear naming
Build and consume internal APIs (e.g., FastAPI) and well-modeled domain libraries (e.g., Pydantic), with attention to clear interfaces and separation of concerns
Participate actively in code review, both giving and receiving feedback, as a core part of how the team ships software
Contribute to the team’s automated test suites and help keep them fast, reliable, and meaningful
Help maintain and improve CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions) so that changes ship safely and frequently
Integrate the software you build with the firm’s data platform (Snowflake) and orchestration (Prefect) where the work calls for it
Write and keep current the technical documentation and runbooks for the components you own
Collaborate with quantitative researchers and fellow engineers to turn requirements into reliable, well-designed software
Participate in agile team practices including sprint planning, backlog grooming, and estimation
Continuously sharpen your engineering practice and take on increasing scope and ownership as you grow
Skills and Knowledge Required
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related quantitative field
At least 1 year of hands-on professional experience writing production software (internships and co-ops can count toward this)
Solid proficiency in Python, including a working understanding of idiomatic, well-structured code
Familiarity with writing automated tests and an understanding of why testing matters.
Familiarity with version control in Git, including branching and the pull-request / code-review workflow
Understanding of core software engineering fundamentals: data structures, clean code, modular design, and debugging
Working proficiency in SQL
Demonstrated ability to learn new technologies quickly and a genuine eagerness to do so
Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to work effectively on a collaborative team
Skills and Knowledge Desired
Exposure to test-driven development and an interest in software craftsmanship (e.g., Clean Code, refactoring, working effectively with legacy code)
Experience building web APIs, ideally with FastAPI or a similar framework
Experience with data modeling and validation libraries such as Pydantic
Exposure to CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions) and modern deployment practices
Familiarity with Azure or another major cloud provider, and with containerization (Docker)
Exposure to a cloud data warehouse (ideally Snowflake) and/or workflow orchestration (Prefect, Dagster, Airflow)
Interest in financial markets, quantitative investing, or financial/market data (no prior finance experience required)
This is a hybrid position based in Los Angeles, CA which requires weekly attendance.

Job Description
Contribute to the org-wide shift from product-specific search solutions to a composable, agent-native infrastructure foundation that agents and applications build on to locate, search, discover, and recommend resources across heterogeneous enterprise data.
Build and own the infrastructural substrate beneath the agentic search platform, spanning the index engine, the ingestion and enrichment pipeline, and the entity, identity, and feature intelligence that gives content context. Solve the hard problem of keeping index-time enrichments aligned with what agents expect at query time, so retrieval, ranking, and reasoning all build on a consistent foundation.
Build and operate hybrid indexing technology at scale across large clusters, spanning keyword-based sparse-vector indices, embedding-based semantic indices, and emerging semantic-ID indexing driven by next-token prediction. Own the full index lifecycle, and expose clean, unified contracts to the search primitives and recipes that agents compose on top of the corpus.

Orchestrate the stages that make content agent-ready, including parsing, chunking, embedding, entity resolution, and access control, and evolve them as new agentic use cases emerge.

Represent each modality so it is retrievable through a unified surface, letting agents find the right material regardless of its form or source.
Contribute to a knowledge graph that resolves entities across enterprise data sources, letting agents link disparate resources such as tickets, files, and people through canonical entity relationships.
Improve the performance, scalability, and observability of search, including query latency, indexing throughput, and cluster health, to deliver low-latency, high-quality agentic search experiences. Apply techniques such as vector quantization to balance model quality, retrieval performance, and storage cost.
Own search infrastructure end to end, from intake and design through rollout and ongoing operations, and help shape the search roadmap as the platform grows to support new agents, primitives, and recipes, including needs not yet anticipated.
Drive reliability and operability across the platform through index lifecycle policies, capacity planning, and cluster scaling strategies that keep a growing library of reusable search capabilities healthy in production.

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.
This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.
Role Overview
As a Software Engineer on the Security Engineering team at Harvey, you'll build and operate foundational security services for both our customer-facing product and the internal systems our workforce depends on: identity and access management, secrets and privileged access, agent sandboxes, and tooling that makes the secure path the fast path. You'll turn security needs into production systems and own the reliability and security of what you build, working closely with engineers and partner teams along the way. Attackers increasingly operate at agent speed, so we’re building defenses that can keep pace.
Security at Harvey is an engineering discipline, not a gatekeeper function. We build platforms and libraries that make it hard for engineers to get security wrong, and we measure ourselves on adoption and outcomes rather than tickets filed. Our program is informed by risk: we invest where the actual exposure to our most sensitive data and resources is greatest, rather than where a framework tells us to.

Build and operate Harvey’s core identity and access services across customer-facing product, workforce, and infrastructure systems, including authentication, authorization, access governance, secrets, and privileged access
Evolve how Harvey customers set up and manage their environments, making security-critical configuration—from identity and access to policies and integrations—delightful to use and secure by default
Build identity controls, sandboxes, and safety harnesses that let services and AI agents operate with least privilege, constrained actions, clear auditability, and effective monitoring
Create secure-by-default libraries, paved-road abstractions, self-service tooling, and agentic workflows that automate security triage, remediation, and evidence collection
Take security systems from design through production, accounting for trust boundaries, attacker paths, and operational failure modes while owning their reliability and security
Share an on-call rotation for Harvey’s mission-critical security services, contribute to incident response, and raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and clear documentation
What You Have
2+ years of software engineering experience, including experience shipping and operating production services
Experience building or contributing to security infrastructure such as identity and access management, authentication and authorization, secrets management, or privileged access
Strong programming, debugging, testing, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work across unfamiliar systems and domains
Experience with cloud infrastructure such as Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, or Amazon Web Services and familiarity with modern distributed-system patterns
A track record of translating security requirements into maintainable, automated systems
Experience using agentic coding tools and creating workflows that automate repetitive security work, with the judgment to review their output critically and measure whether they improve security outcomes
Clear communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to explain technical risks, decisions, and tradeoffs to engineering partners
Working knowledge of common vulnerability classes and the ability to reason about how a system fails under an attacker, not just under load

Experience securing agentic or AI-powered systems, especially systems that act on behalf of users against sensitive data

Qumulo is a software-defined cloud data platform. Our core is a distributed storage operating system in C & Rust, holding exabytes in the datacenter, at the edge, and natively in the cloud. Qumulo serves everything from a hospital's medical imaging archive to an animation studio's render farm in an environment where 99% correct doesn’t cut it.
About the Role:
Joining us, you'd learn and work across our distributed storage engine and the services that help customers store, manage, and protect their data, under the guidance of experienced senior engineers.
This includes a fault-tolerant block layer that erasure-codes and distributes data beneath the file system, a transactional file system where aggregates roll up as they change so a query across billions of files answers in real time instead of walking a tree, and that same machinery drives quotas, capacity trends, snapshot policy, multiple access protocols, plus replication and backup - all running in userspace.
All of which makes Qumulo a distributed operating system problem: scheduling, memory hierarchy, protection, and concurrency. We're AI-forward and specific about what that means. You will learn to use agents to help write code while developing your engineering judgment to ensure every design decision is correct, because nothing ships that isn't right.
Why join Qumulo:
Qumulo blends the flexibility of a startup with the security of a mature and profitable organization. Here you’ll work closely with a small team of smart, capable engineers who will serve as your mentors. Opinions are expected, disagreement is normal, and you'll get hands-on experience taking projects from ideation to release. We value quality, correctness, and performance. Our architecture, protocols, and patents are public, so you can read how most of this works before you talk to us - and we’re small enough that the work you do will actually show up in the product.
As a Software Engineer at Qumulo, you will:
Collaborate with team members on design, code reviews, and pair programming to deliver high-quality software.
Collaborate with team members and area leads on architecture and design of new/updated features.
Contribute to full-lifecycle feature development and testing using C, Rust, and Python.
Take ownership of defining and implementing customer-facing features and internal system improvements.
Help debug, troubleshoot, and fix test failures and complex product or service issues in production environments.
What we're looking for:
Recently graduated (or graduating within the next 9 months) with a degree in Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent experience.
Ability to write well-factored, maintainable, and well-tested code.
Strong grasp of algorithms and data structures, with solid academic or project experience in distributed systems, database concepts, concurrent programming, or operating systems concepts.
Proficiency in C, C++, Rust, Java, or Go demonstrated through classes, internships, or personal projects
Willingness to work collaboratively with a team to solve complex problems and learn quickly on the job.
Ability to work a hybrid schedule from our downtown Seattle HQ
Must be authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or transfer. This role is hybrid, based at our downtown Seattle HQ, targeting 3 days a week in-office.
The salary range for this role is USD $110,000 - $140,000 annual base salary plus pre-IPO stock options and benefits. Individual compensation depends on factors such as role level, relevant experience, and skill set.
Benefits & Perks:
Pre-IPO stock options
Flexible time-off policy
HSA and PPO health insurance options
Dental and Vision insurance
401(k) plan
Choice of an ORCA card or parking subsidy
About Qumulo:
Built for the most demanding enterprise workloads, from AI and HPC simulations to Splunk Observability, genomics and PACS medical imaging, geospatial datasets, media editing and rendering, and video surveillance, Qumulo unlocks the full power of an organization’s information. Our platform unifies file and object storage across data centers, edge, and public clouds, enabling efficient, accelerated computing and extending the reach of data unbound by protocol or transport limitations.
With more than 1,100 customers and exabytes of data under management, Qumulo powers mission-critical workloads anywhere real-time access to massive file datasets is non-negotiable. Qumulo delivers radical simplicity, hardware freedom, exceptional customer support, and a true hybrid-cloud architecture.
Our Values:
At Qumulo, we are building an open and collaborative culture where people can do their best work with customers as our magnetic field. We act as owners, we share by default, we are data driven and experimental and as an inclusive workplace, we encourage and celebrate multiple points of view. As part of our culture we believe diversity drives innovation.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.
WIRELESS SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK)
At SpaceX, we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.
As a Wireless Software Engineer on these programs, you will be solving a wide range of novel engineering challenges:
Firmware, embedded, and signal processing software running on custom hardware that flies the world’s largest fleet of spacecraft.
Cutting-edge networking algorithms capable of connecting thousands of satellites to millions of users in real time.
Infrastructure and tools enabling a highly reliable, software-defined global network.
Our Software Engineers are responsible for the complete lifecycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and support.
Responsibilities
Design, implement, test, and maintain physical and MAC layer software of the wireless software stack for the Starlink communications network.
Participate in architecting current and next-gen Starlink hardware and signal processing algorithms.
Participate in hardware bring-up, debugging, verification and launch.
Work with other teams for cross-layer integration of the end-to-end system.
Develop prototypes to prove out key design concepts and quantify technical constraints.
Collaborate with other engineers to plan and organize the development of our products.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, math, or STEM discipline; OR 2+ years of professional software engineering experience, programming with C or C++ in lieu of a degree.
Experience working with wireless software or network protocols.
Preferred Skills And Experience
Strong knowledge of wireless communications, signal processing and/or network protocols.
Knowledge of RF systems and fundamentals: noise figure, link budget, non-linearity.
Experience writing software for RF/mixed-signal integrated circuits and/or systems, such as phase-locked loops, mixers, data-converters, RF attenuators.
Familiar with design and implementation of Digital Signal Processing algorithms and techniques: FFT, time and frequency domain equalizer, channel estimation, pilot tracking, digital pre-distortion, doppler compensation.
Experience with lab equipment such as RF spectrum analyzer, network analyzer, signal generator, oscilloscope.
Experience in any of physical and/or MAC layers in broadband access technologies such as: Wi-Fi, LTE, 5G or satellite broadband.
Creative approach to problem solving, exceptional analytical skills and engineering fundamentals.
Strong skills in debugging, performance optimization, and unit testing.
Excellent communication skills both written and verbal.
Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements.
Additional Requirements
Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.
Pay Range
COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:
Software Engineer/Level I: $125,000.00 - $145,000.00/per year
Software Engineer/Level II: $145,000.00 - $175,000.00/per year
Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.
Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees in Washington State accrue paid sick time in compliance with state and federal law. JOB SUMMARY
Apptronik is seeking a Robotics Test Engineer to join the Software Integration & Test (RSIT) team. In this role, you will write the automated tests that verify Apollo's software at the integration layer, partner with senior engineers on defect investigations, and help grow the regression coverage that keeps each release safer than the last. You will work hands-on with our pytest-based test infrastructure, HIL benches, and the broader RSIT platform to turn software-level requirements into verifiable tests. Test Authoring: Write automated integration, contract, and ICD conformance tests in pytest against software-level requirements, with clear pass/fail signals that feed the release gate.
Defect Investigation: Partner with senior engineers on root-cause investigations for CI failures, escaped defects, and stochastic issues, building familiarity with debugging tools (sanitizers, log analysis, MCAP playback) over time.
Regression Coverage: Convert defects into permanent regression tests, ensuring every escape becomes a new automated check in the gate.
HIL Test Execution: Run and maintain test suites on hardware-in-the-loop benches, capture data, and report results into the team's dashboards and result reporting systems.
Test Suite Maintenance: Keep existing test suites healthy: triage flaky tests, update fixtures as the stack evolves, and improve readability and reliability of test code.
Requirements Engagement: Read software-level requirements and Systems Validation plans, ask clarifying questions, and surface ambiguity or untestable language to senior teammates and Systems Engineering.
Tooling Feedback: Serve as an active customer of the RSIT platform, surfacing friction in CI, dashboards, or release tooling so the Release & Integration team can improve developer experience.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with stack engineers, firmware engineers, and senior RSIT teammates to understand the systems being tested and produce verification that reflects how those systems actually behave.
SKILLS AND REQUIREMENTS
Programming: Working proficiency in Python, including ability to write clean, maintainable test code and small utility scripts. Comfort reading C++ to understand the systems under test.
Test Frameworks: Hands-on experience with pytest or an equivalent framework (unit test, Google Test, JUnit), including fixtures, parameterization, and test organization.

Communication: Ability to write clear bug reports, test documentation, and pull request descriptions. Comfort asking questions and surfacing blockers early.
Learning Orientation: Eagerness to grow into deeper expertise in robotics, real-time systems, and verification engineering through mentorship, code review, and hands-on work.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.
APPLICATION SOFTWARE ENGINEER
The application software team is the central nervous system of SpaceX – we create mission critical applications that are used throughout SpaceX to accelerate launch vehicle production and flight as well as systems that allow Starlink to grow into a worldwide fast, reliable Internet service. We are looking for engineers who treat fellow teammates with fairness, respect, and support.
Our team is currently creating and evolving systems to enable rapid build and reuse of Starship as well as designing the next generation manufacturing software that will be used in high throughput factories for Starlink. Other applications range from platforms that support concurrent streams of data from many always-on assets to manage the world’s largest satellite constellation to public facing systems where customers can join our Starlink network globally. We work closely with engineers throughout the company to create and update our systems with respect to crewed launches, Starship flights, changes to the Starlink network and much more.
Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, respectful, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission. You will have full ownership of challenging problems, working with a team of enthusiastic engineers with diverse perspectives to design and produce solutions that enable SpaceX to move towards our goals at a rapid pace. The success of the missions at SpaceX depends on the software that you and your team produce.
Responsibilities
Develop highly reliable software solutions that are used across SpaceX
Create new applications that improve how SpaceX operates
Build prototypes to prove out key design concepts and quantify technical constraints
Own all aspects of software engineering and product development
Deep dive into your users’ problems to find and create efficient solutions
Bring your voice to the table in team collaborations on architecture, design, and code reviews
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or scientific discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience building software in lieu of a degree
1+ years of experience in full stack development
Preferred Skills And Experience
Programming experience in Python, C#.NET, Go, Scala, Java, or similar object-oriented language
1+ years of rigorous experience building single page web applications
Experience with version control, continuous integration, and continuous delivery concepts
Expertise in designing software systems
Deep understanding of testing, continuous integration, build, deployment & monitoring
Expertise in profiling and improving application performance
Experience with build systems (Make, Bazel/Pants/Buck, Gradle) and package management tools (pip, npm)
Experience with UNIX-like operating systems and tools like Terraform, Ansible, Puppet for managing them
Experience working with in-stream data processing using Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, or similar technologies
Production experience with Docker and Kubernetes
Front-end experience in Angular, React, or similar JavaScript framework
Database experience with PostgreSQL, SQL Server, or similar database technologies
Additional Requirements
You may be asked to work extended hours/weekends dependent on launch cadence
This role requires you to be onsite. Remote and/or hybrid work will not be considered
Compensation And Benefits
Pay Range:
Level 1: $125,000.00 - $165,000.00
Level 2: $145,000.00 - $200,000.00
Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.
Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees in Washington State accrue paid sick time in compliance with state and federal law. Company shuttles are offered to employees for roundtrip travel from select Seattle locations to the SpaceX Redmond office Monday to Friday.

1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

FLIGHT SOFTWARE INFRASTRUCTURE ENGINEER (STARLINK)
As an infrastructure engineer on the Starlink flight software team, you will be responsible for the software that enables rapid iteration and deployment of both ground and satellite software. You will look for slowdowns in developer iteration, inefficiencies in the build system, and unnecessary interface complexity, and fix them. You will engage closely with other Starlink engineers to identify the biggest challenges they are facing and resolve them. You will be responsible for the full lifecycle of the software that you write, from conception to test to maintenance. Your relentless commitment to streamlining the flight software ecosystem will be critical to the team’s ability to rapidly deliver high quality software.
Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on an inspiring mission.

Maintain flight code generation tooling for flight software and GNC engineers
Maintain core flight software features that are shared across various satellite products
Work closely with flight software developers to understand slow / error prone aspects of embedded software development and fix them
Invent tools and processes that enable fast, accurate, and easy-to-use development and operational systems
Engage ground software teams to understand where flight systems should be changed to simplify constellation operations
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or STEM discipline OR 2+ years of experience in software development
Development experience in C/C++, Python, or other similar programming languages
Preferred Skills And Experience
Knowledge of Bazel, C++, Python, Bash
Experience identifying and improving performance bottlenecks, both in build systems and in embedded environments
Experience designing aesthetic and easy-to-use user interfaces targeted at software engineers
Experience designing fault tolerant, distributed, or real-time embedded systems
Experience with version control, continuous integration, and continuous delivery systems
Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements
Ability to communicate effectively across teams in a solution-oriented manner
Ability to work independently or in a team
Additional Requirements
Willing to work extended hours and weekends when needed
Compensation And Benefits
Pay Range:
Level 1: $125,000.00 - $165,000.00
Level 2: $145,000.00 - $200,000.00

https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/44621.description_preview:
Description
Marketing Measurement and Performance Science (MAPS) measures the incremental impact of Amazon's marketing investments on customer perception, action, and purchases — covering billions in annual fixed marketing (FM) spend across the full funnel. Our outputs provide spend insights and recommendations that power total investment decisions at the S-team level for OP planning, BU-level budget allocation, and in-year spend guidance.
As an SDE II, you'll design and build the systems that transform and harmonize data from 20+ external partners — each with their own schemas, grains, cadences, and nuances — into the measurement-grade inputs that power COSMOS, Amazon's FM causal measurement framework. The problems you will coverage go beyond standard ETL responsibilities — you'll build AI-native systems that reconcile providers with incompatible definitions, handle split metric ownership, manage retroactive revisions, and maintain the immutable snapshots and deterministic joins that causal inference demands.
Key job responsibilities
Design, develop, and maintain measurement-grade data systems at scale — ingesting, standardizing, and vending marketing data from 20+ external and internal sources that feed causal modeling and MLOps systems.
Own full lifecycle delivery of production software on complex, ambiguous problems — from design through launch and ongoing operations — with independence and minimal guidance.
Build automated validation pipelines and data quality frameworks that enforce contracts, detect anomalies across providers, and ensure measurement-grade integrity at every stage.
Define statistical methods for outlier detection, diagnose root causes systematically, and determine corrective actions to maintain data trust.
Partner across science, product, and engineering teams to scope solutions, navigate constraints, and ship the most efficient path from prototype to production.
Write clean, well-tested code (Python, Scala, or Java) and mentor junior engineers on system design, code quality, and operational best practices.
A day in the life
Day to day, you'll build and scale multi-layer automated validation pipelines, with clear data lineage so every model run is fully reproducible. Our vision is to scale our infrastructure across new business units and geographies reaching 90%+ coverage of Amazon's FM spend, and develop self-service catalog and observability tooling that lets scientists and partner teams explore our data without filing tickets. You'll also have a direct influence on schema governance — designing systems that enforce data standards at the point of contract, detect drift from providers, and keep our specifications current as partnerships expand.
You'll collaborate closely with causal scientists, economists, product managers, and agency data ops teams — translating measurement requirements into scalable technical solutions. This is a high-ownership role where your work directly determines whether Amazon's leadership can trust the numbers behind billion-dollar marketing investment decisions.
About The Team
Within MAPS, the Marketing Inputs & Data Automation (MIDA) team owns the measurement-grade data layer that sets the ceiling on what our causal models can measure, where they can operate, and how confident leadership should be in the outputs. We build and operate large-scale data infrastructure and data assets — ingesting, validating, harmonizing, and vending data from 20+ third-party providers (agencies, aggregators, publishers) across multiple Amazon business units and marketing channels, with global coverage. Our pipeline is purpose-built for the high bar of causal inference — not dashboards or reporting — requiring strict temporal integrity, historical stability, multi-layer validation, full lineage, and reproducibility at every stage.
Basic Qualifications
3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience

ProEdge Dental Water Labs is a team of selfless builders. By putting our focus on the success of customers, we've created a healthy, quickly-growing, dynamic company. Our ~50 team has taken on a significant challenge: transform compliance in the dental practice—an often distinct pain for our customers—into a culture of shared purpose for the safety of patients and staff. By building trust and developing value-based solutions, we've created an emerging brand in dental.
Because of that, "good work" is the floor here. What we're building takes people who care more about the mission than the credit, who tell the truth before it's comfortable, and who would rather be stretched by real responsibility than protected from it.
Our Values
We build trust—by speaking candidly, doing what we say, and owning our mistakes.
We serve the team above ourselves—by choosing the mission over comfort, clarifying expectations, and engaging in feedback.
We delight our customers—by taking ownership of their experience, delivering quality they can count on, and treating every customer as valuable.
We create clarity—by making the goal plain, speaking up when we don't know, and closing the loop when clarity is at risk.
We improve—by driving our own growth, fixing the root, and making the better way repeatable.
The Software Engineer II Opportunity
Thousands of dental practices, from single offices to the largest dental groups in the country, use ProEdge's compliance platform to test their waterlines and sterilizers, see their results, and prove to inspectors that patients are safe. Inside sales and Customer Success work from data and reports built for them inside the platform, with a first cut in use within 120 days.

Production is observable and safe: error tracking and alerting live, runbooks for the top failure modes, secrets in a managed store, and no critical or high dependency findings, within 90 days.

Direct AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, or whatever is best next quarter) to build, then read every diff, write the tests, and own the result in production. Nobody will ask you to prove you can type it by hand; everybody will ask how you know it works.

Write Playwright end-to-end tests, API permission tests, and SQL tests around a compliance engine built from stored procedures and triggers, and keep the merge gate green as the team's source of truth.
Build and own the delivery platform on AWS (App Runner, Amplify Hosting, RDS, infrastructure as code with CDK): rolling deploys, rollback, monitoring, alerting, and managed secrets.
Ship the reporting, data views, and exports the inside sales and Customer Success teams need, and sit with the people who use them.
Own the platform's integrations: HubSpot for email, NetSuite for orders, the API our largest dental-group customers build on, and the data platform our BI team reports from.
Write it down: decision records, runbooks, and a living map of the system, plus the conventions and context files that let an agent or a new engineer be productive in the repo in minutes.
Share an on-call rotation with the Head of Technology once production is instrumented, and be steady when it misbehaves.

Daily use of AI coding agents as your primary way of building, and the ability to show us your workflow live, including how you review, test, and correct what the agent produces.

Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”
Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.
The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.
About The Role
Health system call centers can't keep up with patient demand. 85% of patients who can't get through never call back. They go elsewhere, and appointments that should have been booked never are.
We're building AI Voice Agents that pick up every call and handle the full conversation: scheduling, rescheduling, cancellations, confirmations, FAQs, and intake. They work by integrating directly with the EHR and telephony stack in real time.
We're hiring a Software Engineer to build the systems these agents run on: the voice pipelines, EHR integrations, and services that take a call from "hello" to a booked appointment. It's a mid-level role on a small team that ships every day, with a lot of room to grow into harder problems.
This full-time position requires working 5 days a week in our Mountain View, CA office.
What You'll Do
Build backend services in Python that power real-time voice agents: call orchestration, conversation state, tool execution, and EHR write-back.
Contribute to low-latency pipelines connecting telephony, ASR, LLMs, and TTS into a single conversational loop.
Integrate with healthcare systems (like Epic, Cerner, athena, and others) for scheduling, eligibility, and intake.
Collaborate with senior engineers to design APIs, data models, and event-driven workflows.
Partner with AI, product, and operations to ship features patient access teams actually use.
Own the quality of what you ship: latency, reliability, observability, and release readiness.
What You Have
2–4 years of backend software experience, primarily in Python.
Experience shipping production services, APIs, and data models.
An intuition for how people interact with automated assistants through voice and text, where the rules are different than icons and buttons.
Comfort with async, event-driven, or real-time systems (or excitement to grow into them).
Strong fundamentals in testing, LLM evaluation, observability, and reliability.
A patient centered mindset. You design for the person on the other end of the line, not just the metrics.
Bias for action and an ownership mindset.

Product sense. You care how it feels to use, not only that it works

Browser use / computer use, or browser automation (Playwright, Puppeteer, CDP)
Voice, video, or anything real-time (WebRTC a plus)
Go-to-market / sales-tech tooling, automations, or exposure to the sales workflow
Scraping, enrichment, or data pipelines

We're a fast-moving team. We want AI-native builders who work differently and produce the output of a much larger team — people here for the ride and the mission, not just pay and stability.

Small enough that everything you build matters, and you'll watch it run in real sales calls

Our Science & Technology directorates include National Security, Earth and Biological Sciences, Physical and Computational Sciences, and Energy and Environment. The National Security Directorate (NSD) drives science-based, mission-focused solutions to take on complex, real-world threats to our nation and the world.
The Physical Detection Systems and Deployment Division, part of the National Security Directorate, delivers policy-informed technology solutions by removing barriers to real-world implementation. The Advanced Engineered Systems group within PNNL builds embedded electronic systems to support various applications including imaging systems, system health monitoring, cyber security and advanced radio frequency devices to sense and communicate with other devices. The applicant is expected to apply fundamentals of electrical engineering to test custom electronic and RF printed circuit boards, work with software defined radios (SDR) and custom software to verify functionality. The applicant will also learn RF fundamentals to set up and test RF sensing and interrogation devices. C/C++ and python software languages will be extensively used to automate tasks, collect data from analog and digital systems and deliver data to modern computing systems. Executing ad-hoc and defined test cases and critical thinking is fundamental to this position to confirm proper system operation in real world environments. Basic knowledge of command line and remote access to Linux operating systems is crucial to success as well as electronics fundamentals to troubleshoot and correct issues with custom printed circuit boards. The position also may entail working with data scientists to configure and deploy hardware for machine learning applications, such as NVIDIA Jetson GPUs, FPGAs and custom and commercial accelerators. The job duties will give the applicant an opportunity to experience electrical and computer engineering fundamentals as applied to real-world applications in a research environment, while assisting in missions that make our nation safer.
Key Responsibilities
Write software test utilities in C/C++ and python
Configure SDR and RF systems for testing
Collect and analyze data
Read schematics, test circuits and develop small circuits to meet various system needs
Configure electronic systems for system validation and testing
Test electronic systems for performance verification

Basic scripting/software development experience in C/C++ and/or Python.
Familiarity with Linux operating systems and command line interfaces.
Basic electronic circuit theory and ability to read schematics.

Familiarity with virtualized containers: Docker, VMware, etc.
Basic electronic circuit theory and familiarity with datasheets.
Familiarity with Linux operating systems and command line interfaces.

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. SPACE SYSTEMS
At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. MACHINE LEARNING ENGINEER II

Field AI is transforming how robots interact with the real world. We are building risk-aware, reliable, and field-ready AI systems that address the most complex challenges in robotics, unlocking the full potential of embodied intelligence. We go beyond typical data-driven approaches or pure transformer-based architectures, and are charting a new course, with already-globally-deployed solutions delivering real-world results and rapidly improving models through real-field applications.
Systems Engineer Role
As a Systems Engineer on the Hardware Team at Field AI, you will bring new robot platforms into our fleet and ensure that they operate at high standards in real world environments. This will involve integrating our control systems, autonomy stack, and payloads onto new robotic platforms. Your work will span across areas including platform abstraction, robot control, autonomy, sim-to-real validation, and electro-mechanical integration.
Responsibilities may include the full lifecycle from initial platform bring-up through safety qualification and field deployment. You will collaborate closely with the Autonomy/RL, Manipulation, Mechanical, and Electrical teams to build tightly integrated solutions ready for deployment in challenging field environments. Additionally while your focus will be on platform integration, you may contribute across hardware, field operations, and autonomy domains.
What You Will Get To Do
1. Platform Integration & Controls
Platform Abstraction:
Build software abstraction layers between each robot's native control stack (such as ROS/ROS2) and our own systems, enabling payloads to move across platforms.
Robot Controls & Navigation:
Ensure navigation and controls stacks running correctly on physical hardware across quadruped, humanoid, and wheeled platforms.
Electro-Mechanical Integration:
Work with mechanical and electrical engineers on designing and integrating mechanical (saddles) and electrical (power distributions boards) interfaces .
Sim-to-Real:
Validate and adapt RL-based autonomy policies from simulation (Isaac, Gazebo, MuJoCo) to real-world performance on terrain, stairs, and uneven ground.
2. Cross-Team Collaboration & Fleet Scaling
Cross-Functional Integration:
Coordinate across Autonomy/RL, Manipulation, Mechanical, and Electrical teams to bring new platforms online.
Testing & Validation:
Use SIL/HIL testing to ensure integrated systems are safe, reliable, and ready for field operation. Test features such as safety features and operations under different Operational Design Domains (ODDs).
New Robots:
Identify, procure, test, and integrate diverse new robotic systems.
Multi-Platform Support:
Support multiple robot morphologies including legged, quadruped, biped/humanoid, and wheeled UGVs.
3. Safety & Infrastructure
Safety Systems:
Implement e-stop and redundancy/fault-tolerant safety layers, contributing to functional safety (ISO 26262, ASIL) as practices mature.
Charging & Docking Infrastructure:
Support charging station and docking infrastructure for charging, data offload, and communications.
Field Deployment Logistics:
Handle the hands-on logistics of standing up new robot platforms for field deployment across construction, mining, and oil & gas environments.
What You Have
Education:
B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field.
Experience Level:
We are looking to fill this role with someone with 3-9 years of experience.
Software:
Hands-on experience with middleware (ROS/ROS2) and computing languages (python, C++).
Robotics Software Generalist:
Strong generalist robotics software background spanning controls, navigation, and systems integration across legged and wheeled platforms.
Sim-to-Real Experience:
Comfort working across the sim-to-real gap, validating RL or autonomy policies from simulation (Isaac, Gazebo, MuJoCo) on physical hardware.
Cross Functional Hardware Knowledge:
Working familiarity with motors, actuation, BLDC motor controllers, and power distribution or electrical systems.
Communication Protocols:
Familiarity with CAN bus, EtherCAT, or similar real-time robotics communication protocols.
Systems Thinking:
Ability to work across mechanical, electrical, controls, and autonomy domains to make integrated systems function reliably on real hardware.
What Will Set You Apart
Multi-Platform Experience:
Experience integrating software across multiple robot platforms, including legged/quadruped, humanoid, and wheeled UGVs (e.g., Unitree, Boston Dynamics, Clearpath).
Field Environments:
Experience deploying robots in harsh, diverse industrial field environments such as construction, mining, and oil & gas.
Functional Safety:
Background in functional safety standards (ISO 26262, ASIL, SOTIF/ISO 21448) and safety-critical systems testing and validation.
Advanced Controls:
Experience with whole-body control, impedance/admittance control, MPC, or trajectory optimization for legged or manipulator systems.
Fleet & Infrastructure:
Experience with multi-robot fleet operations, auto-docking/charging infrastructure, or teleoperation systems

EDA R&D Engineer (C++, AI for Physical Design)
This is not a conventional Physical Design Engineer role. If your experience is primarily running P&R flows, even expertly and at advanced nodes, this probably isn't the one.
We're working with an early-stage semiconductor software company building AI-native optimization technology for backend chip implementation. The technology works alongside existing commercial EDA flows and tackles PPA optimization directly.
They're building a small founding engineering team with significant technical ownership and multiple positions open.
The strongest candidates demonstrate at least two of three areas:
EDA tool development
You've written production software inside EDA/CAD technology — placement, routing, timing, synthesis, DRC/physical verification, optimization algorithms or design-space exploration. We're looking for C/C++ development of the underlying technology, rather than simply scripts or flows around commercial tools.
Applied AI/ML
You've built or deployed models, agents, reinforcement learning or other ML/AI techniques against real engineering problems.
Exceptional physical design depth
You understand placement, routing, congestion, timing closure, PPA and/or physical verification deeply enough to understand why implementation tools behave the way they do — not simply how to operate them.
Two of the three is enough. Nobody is expected to have all three.
Backgrounds that fit
We're particularly interested in engineers from EDA vendor R&D teams, internal CAD/tool-development groups, semiconductor R&D organizations, university CAD research and technically ambitious startups.
Experience at an EDA vendor alone isn't enough. Application engineering, flow development and commercial-tool usage are different from developing the underlying EDA technology.
Startup experience is a plus, as is evidence that you've built something from scratch.
Seniority
We're deliberately flexible. Around 2–3 years of relevant industry experience is a useful starting point, but exceptional graduate researchers and engineers earlier in their careers are genuinely in scope. Experienced Senior/Staff engineers who remain deeply technical are equally relevant.
There is no specific PhD requirement. Technical profile matters more than years or academic pedigree.

Bay Area Peninsula, approximately four days onsite

$250,000–$350,000 base + meaningful early-stage equity

Available

Available

Multiple positions

build the tools rather than simply use them
, particularly where EDA, optimization, physical design and AI intersect, we'd like to hear from you.

About the Role
We are looking for a Systems Performance Modeling Engineer to build the models and tools that predict how generative AI inference workloads perform on Tensordyne systems, from a single accelerator up through rack, pod, and cluster scale. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who likes writing simulator code, running experiments, and digging into why a prediction and a measurement don't match.
Working closely with our architects and the silicon, hardware, networking, and software teams, you'll capture workload behavior, extend simulation and analytical models of our silicon, interconnect, and multi-hop fabrics, and validate them against real hardware. You'll be comfortable moving across the stack, from the model graph through collectives to the network fabric, to track down where performance is going.

Model collective communication on multi-hop scale-out fabrics, including implementing custom collective algorithms designed for our topology.
Run calibration experiments on Tensordyne hardware as systems come up, compare them against model predictions, and fix the sources of error.

Strong programming skills in C++ and Python, with clean, testable, maintainable code.

Clear written and verbal communication, especially when presenting data and trade-offs to other engineers.
MS or higher in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.

Publications or open-source contributions in ML systems, architecture, or networking.

Motion planning

Control

Manipulation

Interest in Active Inference or Machine Learning.

About The Role
Endeavor's Platform team builds the data, tools, and AI infrastructure that powers our global network across 50+ markets. With Claude Enterprise now deployed to 390+ staff across 43+ markets, access to AI is no longer our constraint. The next challenge is organizational: converting that access into institutional capabilities that one team can build, another market can reuse, and Endeavor retains when people move on.
We're looking for a
curious, hands-on, builder-minded intern
to help create Endeavor's
AI organizational infrastructure
: the reusable capabilities, templates, governance rails, and enablement systems that let our local offices and functional teams design their own AI-augmented processes safely and effectively, instead of 50 markets reinventing the same tools in isolation.
This is not a shadowing role. It is a hybrid role between discovery and applied AI engineering. You will interview local offices and functional departments to understand their workflows and what infrastructure they actually need, and you will get your hands dirty: prototyping agentic workflows, Claude skills, MicroApps, and retrieval systems on Endeavor's enterprise AI stack (Claude Enterprise, MCP integrations, Snowflake, Salesforce, and Notion). You will also support the Platform team's deeper work on knowledge capture and institutional memory, helping turn the network's interactions into structured, trusted, actionable knowledge.
By the end of the internship, you'll have shipped real capabilities used by teams across markets, creating a tangible output with lasting impact on how nearly 500 Endeavor colleagues work worldwide. This internship is ideal for someone excited by applied AI, organizational systems, and building things that scale globally, while gaining real responsibility and visibility inside a mission-driven organization.
Key Responsibilities
Responsibility #1: Discover What Teams Actually Need
Lead structured interviews with local offices and functional departments to map their workflows, pain points, and existing AI experiments. Find where a shared, governed capability would beat fifty isolated ones, and identify what infrastructure, training, or guardrails each team needs to build effectively on their own.
Responsibility #2: Build Reusable AI Capabilities
Prototype agentic workflows, Claude skills, MicroApps, and retrieval features on our enterprise stack (Claude Enterprise, MCP, APIs), always choosing the lightest technical pattern that supports the behavior we want. Package what works so another market can adopt it without rebuilding it.
Responsibility #3: Create the Enablement Infrastructure
Help create the templates, playbooks, starter kits, and documentation that let teams self-serve: how to build a skill, an Artifact, a plugin, etc.; how to connect to governed data and use our MCPs; and how to stay within Endeavor's AI Policy. Make the right way the easy way.
Responsibility #4: Support Knowledge Capture & Institutional Memory
Support the Platform team's work on turning captured knowledge (meetings, founder ratings, network interactions) into structured, actionable intelligence, including retrieval pipelines and early knowledge graph work that makes institutional memory usable at the moment of key decisions.
Responsibility #5: Govern and Evaluate What You Ship
Define what "working" means for the capabilities you build: success metrics, output quality checks, and simple eval loops. Contribute everything to Endeavor's AI Registry so it is human-owned, tracked, permission-aware, and auditable in line with Endeavor's AI Policy.
Skills And Qualifications - Who You Are
Student Status: Undergraduate Junior or Senior, or Graduate student in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems, Business, or a related field; candidates from other disciplines with relevant skills and demonstrated building experience are encouraged to apply.

Experience in data centers, power generation, semiconductor, or other high-reliability industrial environments
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal

Who We Are
EOI Space is developing and deploying a constellation of satellites in Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) to provide ultra-high-resolution Earth imagery. We aim to deliver timely and actionable data for commercial and defense applications.
We're working toward a number of industry firsts, and that takes a team willing to dig into hard problems, get hands-on, and work well together. EOI Space is looking for an Embedded Software Engineer to build the software and firmware that runs on our satellites: embedded Linux on the payload processor, bare-metal control loops on the microcontrollers, and the FPGA logic underneath. We care more about how you think and how fast you learn than whether you've already used our exact toolchain, so deep experience across this stack is great, but solid embedded fundamentals and a real willingness to learn the rest will get our attention too.
What You Will Do
You will design, write, and test the flight software and firmware for our next-generation spacecraft. You will work at the boundary between hardware and software: sitting with electrical engineers during board bring-up, reading schematics and datasheets, and tracing problems down to the register level when needed. You will collaborate across systems engineering, manufacturing, and test to deliver flight-ready software for satellite integration. This is a hands-on role in a lean and collaborative environment, and you will own meaningful pieces of the vehicle early.
Responsibilities
Develop and maintain embedded Linux software on Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ platforms, including Yocto layers and recipes, BSP and device tree work, kernel drivers, and userspace applications
Write and test bare-metal firmware for TI C2000 microcontrollers, including real-time control loops, peripheral configuration, and communications interfaces
Develop and verify FPGA logic in Verilog for Xilinx and Microchip devices, including the interfaces between programmable logic and the processing system
Bring up new hardware alongside our electrical engineers, including first boot, driver bring-up, and debugging with JTAG, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers
Build and improve the tooling that surrounds flight software, including build systems, version control practices, hardware-in-the-loop test benches, and automated regression
Collaborate with systems, electrical, mechanical, and test engineers to ensure software and hardware come together cleanly
Lead root cause investigations and system-level troubleshooting in both lab and on-orbit environments
Develop and maintain technical documentation, including interface control documents (ICDs), register maps, software design descriptions, and test plans
Support integration, environmental test, and launch campaigns, and help operate the software you wrote once it is on orbit
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's Electrical Engineering, Computer Science or equivalent hands-on experience
4-6 years of hands-on embedded software or firmware development. A sharp engineer earlier in their career who learns quickly will be considered alongside candidates with a decade of experience
Strong C, and C++ where it fits, in resource-constrained and real-time environments
Comfort working directly against hardware: reading schematics and datasheets, using JTAG debuggers, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers, and reasoning about what the silicon is actually doing
Experience with, or a demonstrated ability and willingness to ramp quickly on, one or more of: Zynq UltraScale+ with Yocto-based embedded Linux, TI C2000 bare-metal firmware, and Verilog FPGA development for Xilinx and Microchip parts
Comfortable with ambiguity. Much of this work is new, specifications are incomplete, and the right answer is often found by building something and testing it

Escalate rather than improvise when a situation is not covered by a documented standard.

Implement and evaluate defined DSP and 5G NR physical-layer (PHY) functions for satellite communications over non-terrestrial networks (NTN), working from agreed specifications and technical guidance.

Working knowledge of wireless PHY processing and the ability to translate technical specifications into implementation and test cases; familiarity with the basic structure of a 5G NR PHY.
Understanding of fixed-point arithmetic, quantization, overflow, and numerical precision, with the ability to compare an implementation against a reference model.
Understanding of embedded software constraints, including execution time, memory use, and hardware/software interfaces, supported by practical implementation or debugging work.
Ability to build reproducible tests, use version control, document technical assumptions and results, and explain discrepancies during code and design reviews.

Experience with SystemC TLM, or with HLS tools to develop and verify synthesizable C/C++ or SystemC implementations.
Experience with 5G NR or NTN algorithms and specifications, satellite channel modeling, or compensation for Doppler and timing effects.
Experience with FPGA/ASIC verification, emulation, SDR platforms, chip bring-up, or laboratory validation of communication systems.
Experience with 5G NR MAC, PHY/MAC interfaces, scheduling interactions, or HARQ procedures.
Experience implementing and optimizing algorithms on vector DSPs, including SIMD intrinsics, vectorization, and efficient memory access.
Experience with low-power ASIC or firmware design, including reducing computation and data movement, managing idle states, or measuring power consumption.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
About The Team
At Anduril, our Battlespace Awareness Command and Control Software team specializes in solving complex, real-world problems through cutting-edge algorithms and intelligent software integrations. Operating in small, innovative teams, we push the boundaries of what's possible to deliver advanced technologies with mission-critical applications. Our commitment doesn't end with academic research or proof-of-concept experiments; we measure our success by the real-world impact of our deployed solutions. Inspired by Arthur C. Clarke's vision — “Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic” — we aim to achieve groundbreaking results in path planning, route optimization, and autonomous mission execution at the command and control layer. We are currently seeking highly talented technologists to join our mission and redefine the future of defense technology.
What You Will Do
Contribute hands-on to a small, collaborative team within the Command and Control Software organization, applying your growing expertise in path planning and route optimization.
Prototype and help deploy state-of-the-art algorithms for global and local path planning, trajectory optimization, and multi-agent coordination within command and control systems.
Help develop online (real-time) path planning capabilities that replan safely and efficiently as mission conditions, threats, and vehicle states change.
Design and develop high-performance software for real-time C2 systems deployed on operational platforms in the field — from operator-facing mission planning tools to autonomous tasking and routing services that orchestrate fleets of unmanned systems — with a strong emphasis on asynchronous programming, concurrency, and reliable execution in resource-constrained environments.
Implement robust planners, search algorithms, and decision-making systems that generate safe, feasible, and optimal routes in dynamic, uncertain, and contested environments.
Analyze system performance using high-fidelity simulations, modeling tools, and statistical techniques to validate planner behavior across diverse mission scenarios.
Support customer success by developing and implementing algorithms and software for mission-critical use cases, including collaborative autonomy, asset routing, and obstacle and threat avoidance.
Integrate path planning technologies into the broader command and control software stack and development lifecycle, from requirements definition through testing and optimization.
Translate technical progress into clear, actionable insights for diverse stakeholders, including colleagues, operators, and end-users.
Required Qualifications
3+ years of experience in algorithm design, software development, and mathematical modeling with programming expertise in C/C++ and/or Rust.
Strong knowledge of path planning techniques, such as graph-based search (A*, D* Lite), sampling-based planners (RRT, RRT*, PRM), and online/real-time replanning approaches.
Demonstrated experience in guidance, navigation, and control (GNC); trajectory optimization and trajectory prediction; and/or the development of predictive models for vehicle dynamics and weapon system effectiveness (e.g., 6-DoF simulation, intercept analysis).
Solid understanding of applied mathematics, including linear algebra, optimization, computational geometry, and graph theory.
Knowledge of vehicle dynamics, kinematic constraints, and control theory as applied to autonomous ground, air, or maritime platforms tasked through C2 systems, including high-speed aerial vehicles.
Familiarity with map representations, terrain reasoning, state estimation, and the efficient handling of large-scale geospatial and environmental data within distributed C2 architectures.
Exposure to machine learning as applied to planning and decision-making, including reinforcement learning, learned heuristics, and behavior prediction.
Ability to write robust, concurrent code for planning under uncertainty and operation in complex, dynamic, contested environments.
Demonstrated ability to work across development lifecycles, from prototyping to optimizing production systems.
Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.
NICE TO HAVE
Experience with Rust for high-performance, safety-critical software.
Exposure to mixed greenfield/brownfield codebases, including extending an existing planning/routing stack in production.

About Hightouch
Hightouch is an Agentic Marketing Platform powered by the industry-leading Composable CDP. With complete brand context, customer data, and performance history in one place, every marketer finally has the power to build and ship end-to-end campaigns themselves. Teams move faster, stay on brand, and get AI marketing that actually works.
Founded in 2019 and headquartered in San Francisco, Hightouch enables marketing teams to analyze performance, brainstorm ideas, and generate creative at a speed and quality that wasn't previously possible.
Named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Customer Data Platforms, Hightouch is trusted by leading enterprises like Domino's, Spotify, Aritzia, Cars.com, Ramp, and PetSmart.
At Hightouch, our mission is to help our customers leverage data and AI to grow their businesses. The team is ambitious, impact-driven, efficient — and we believe humility, kindness, and compassion are essential to our success. If you're energized by velocity, obsessed with raising the bar, and want to build alongside people who care deeply about each other and our customers, we'd love to meet you.
About The Role
We're looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to own solution design and implementation for our Identity Resolution (IDR) product. This role is a blend of data analytics and data engineering, and is an opportunity to work directly with data, marketing, and executive teams at household-name companies. You'll spend time working with the customer to learn about their data architecture, reason about how Hightouch can accomplish their goals, set up deployments, and debug issues.
This role is hands on and technical. You’ll become intimately familiar with our customers’ data and business goals. This expertise frequently leads to us advising executives at Fortune 500 companies on their long term data strategy. You'll spend time helping customers decide how their global identity spines should be configured, you'll set up implementations for them, and you'll debug inevitable issues with real data. You'll work closely with Sales Engineering on pre-sales deals and with Customer Support Engineering and Technical Account Management on post-sales implementations—serving as the subject matter expert for data engineering and analytics across the customer lifecycle.
You'll work with coding agents as a default: the SQL, schema spelunking, and internal tooling in this role gets built with agents - and you’ll help grow our repository of skills and best practices so we all get faster.
About Hightouch Identity Resolution (IDR)
Imagine you're a sprawling enterprise business with 20+ brands. Each brand collects different data elements from each of their customers and joins using different identifiers. Hightouch IDR can look across the customer data stored in each brand and provide a golden source of truth using all the available data, while obeying any regulatory restrictions that prevent data sharing. The product is highly configurable, and so no two customer data architectures are the same.
What You'll Do
Solution Architecture & Implementation Consulting
Work backwards from end goals: Customers ultimately don't care about IDR itself, but about the use cases that a good identity spine powers. You’ll pair with an architect to work backwards from the customer’s use cases to a set of IDR rules and a data model that enables those use cases
Assess fit and feasibility: During pre-sales, understand the customer’s data landscape and maturity, assessing how much work will be needed to get their data ready for IDR. Understand the rules of any current solutions (e.g., Reltio, Amperity, Segment, MDM tools) and identify, flag, and create workarounds for any gaps.
Technical Support & Debugging
Debug customer issues end-to-end: Investigate perceived issues and discrepancies in identity such as missing datapoints and over-merging scenarios. Most debugging involves writing SQL against customer warehouses and reading server logs.
Explain IDR behavior to customers: Help customers understand how warehouse-native identity resolution works and detailed nuances of how it processes data incrementally or how to utilize its outcome tables.
Surface product gaps: When you see the same issue repeatedly (e.g., no retroactive data removal, insufficient observability into profile changes, inability to reset incremental processing watermarks), flag and advocate for fixes.
What We're Looking For
You direct agents, you don't just prompt them. You'll point them at warehouses with undocumented tables and no reliable dictionary, and you'll be the last judgment before what they build ships to millions of people. You reach for an agent before a blank editor, but you scrutinize every line before it goes out.
SQL Fluency: Anyone can generate a thousand lines of SQL now. You're hired because you can read them and find the join that's wrong. Fluent in Snowflake, Databricks or BigQuery, with query performance and warehouse cost as things you think about unprompted.
Systems thinking: You can reason about how identity graphs behave at scale, understand trade-offs between different architecture choices, and anticipate downstream consequences of design decisions.
Consultative communication: You can run a discovery call, ask the right questions to understand requirements, and explain technical trade-offs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Systematic debugging mindset: You naturally form hypotheses, test them, and document findings. When you see "missing data," you think through timestamps, model definitions, and PK validity before jumping to conclusions.
2-4 years in an analytics engineering, solutions engineering, forward-deployed engineering, or implementation role—ideally at a data infrastructure, CDP, or B2B SaaS company.
Nice to Have
Experience with identity resolution, MDM, or CDP products (Segment, Amperity, Reltio, LiveRamp)
Familiarity with graph data structures and entity resolution algorithms

The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices.
